title: 17th and Kater ballroom in the Red Light district
summary: Miller's regular ballroom was at 17th and Kater, in the heart of South Street's red light district, while the read-music dance band played a high-class hall near Broad Street.

blocks.x: But with Lonnie, Lonnie, we didn't have a regular job. But we played in Philadelphia also. But we played there one night, there one night, you know, like we called it gigs.
Sure. What was the name of the ballroom where you played regularly with Charlie Miller?

Waldorf, something, Castle or something like that. I know where it was, it was 17th and Kater Street in Philadelphia, I know, I remember that real well. And that's down in the Soho district, or what they call - what they call that district? - you know, something like Pigalle or -
Well, all the chicks like it, you know.
All the pimps hang out and everything, that's where we played.
Trying to say it was the Red Light district and -
Red Light district, that's what I'm trying to say. South Street, 17th and Kater was the heart of the Red Light district, know what I mean, right in the middle of it.
And Kater Street, that particular street was considered a very, very bad street, you know. You know, Kater Street, [ ].
The ballroom you were playing with the band that just read music -
Oh, that was up around Broad Street, that was north of -
